terms.definition: Breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful ones.
terms.examiner: Catalytic cracking uses a hot catalyst; steam cracking uses high temperature with steam.

terms.definition: There is more demand for small, useful fuel molecules than crude oil supplies; cracking also makes alkenes for polymers.
terms.examiner: Supply and demand is the standard explanation.

terms.definition: An unsaturated hydrocarbon with a C=C double bond; general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
Orange bromine water turns colourless with an alkene but stays orange with an alkane.
